**Repaired finding submitted: compliant** (no redline).

The only failing item was the deterministic period check, which the verifier confirmed as a false negative: § 19.2 writes the period in words ("ninety days") rather than as a numeral or in months. The repaired rationale now states the period explicitly as **90 days (3 months), measured from the later of delivery or acceptance**, so the ≥ 90-day threshold is evidenced on its face.

Substance unchanged and at or above the preferred position:

- **19.1** — professional/workmanlike standard, qualified personnel, industry standards, plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications.
- **19.2** — 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty from the later of delivery or acceptance; Hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term**, exceeding the 12-month software benchmark for a hosted product.
- **19.3** — no malicious code, Applicable Law compliance, no functionality diminishment, no contaminating open source.
- **19.4** — re-perform / repair / replace at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid; expressly non-exclusive for fraud, IP, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **19.5** — mutual implied-warranty disclaimer that expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy; no "AS IS" exposure.

§ 6 acceptance and § 3.1 do not cut the period short. Noted in the rationale only as a drafting nit: "ninety days" would read better as "ninety (90) days" — not a deviation, so no redline was proposed and the paragraphs remain unchanged.
